- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 3–8% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00), model frequently fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 5–10% in the following 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak (≤0.33) and price is trending upward; increase forecast by 3–7% if sentiment remains low but price is rising.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags behind true price by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average of true values.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast using 5-day weighted average of true values.
- If sentiment is bullish but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid false momentum.
